title: Delhi H1N1 Cases Cross 2,600 as Hospitals Scale Up Isolation Wards
excerpt: India's capital has recorded around 3,000 influenza cases this year, with H1N1 accounting for nearly three-quarters of all Influenza A infections. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has called an emergency review meeting.
body:
• Delhi has recorded around 3,000 influenza cases in 2026, including over 2,600 confirmed H1N1 infections — a nearly sixfold increase from 229 cases during the same period last year
  • Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has called an emergency review meeting; Health Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh says isolation wards are operational across the city
  • ICMR Director-General Rajiv Bahl says the H1N1 strain accounts for 98% of tested Influenza A cases nationally, but the circulating virus shows no signs of being a new or more dangerous strain
  • LNJP Hospital has set up a dedicated isolation ward with a 70-bed backup facility including 10 ICU beds, ready to activate if admissions surge

Delhi's H1N1 influenza count has crossed 2,600 confirmed cases in 2026, prompting Chief Minister Rekha Gupta to convene an emergency meeting to review the city's public health response. The capital has recorded approximately 3,000 total influenza cases this year, with H1N1 — commonly known as swine flu — making up the overwhelming majority.

The numbers represent a sharp escalation. Delhi logged 229 H1N1 cases during the same period last year, making the 2026 figure a nearly sixfold increase. Health officials attribute the surge to seasonal monsoon conditions, increased person-to-person transmission and lower population immunity to the currently circulating influenza variant.

Government Response

Delhi Health Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh told reporters that the situation remained under control, with adequate doctors, medical staff and medicines available at hospitals across the capital.

"There is no shortage of doctors, staff or medicines. The chief minister has called an emergency review meeting. I assure you there is no problem, everything is under control."

Isolation wards have been set up at hospitals across Delhi, which has a population of more than two crore (20 million). The Lok Nayak Jai Prakash Narayan Hospital has established a dedicated seven-bed isolation ward — five high-dependency beds and two ventilated beds — with a 70-bed backup facility on standby.

"If the number of patients increases, we've created a 70-bed ward on the seventh floor, which has 10 ICU beds and 60 HDU beds," said Dr Satyajit Kumar, Head of the Accident and Emergency department at LNJP Hospital.

National Surveillance Picture

Indian Council of Medical Research Director-General Rajiv Bahl said the H1N1 strain has emerged as the dominant respiratory pathogen circulating across India, accounting for nearly 98 per cent of tested Influenza A cases. The circulating viruses have been identified as A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1) pdm09-like viruses, a lineage in continuous circulation in India since 2025.

Bahl emphasised that the genetic changes observed in the viruses are consistent with normal antigenic drift seen in seasonal influenza and do not indicate the emergence of a new or dangerous strain. India's multi-tiered surveillance network — linking state-level data through the Integrated Health Information Platform and the National Centre for Disease Control, layered with hospital-based sampling by ICMR — continues to monitor the situation in real time.

Who Is at Risk

H1N1 is a subtype of Influenza A that has circulated as a seasonal human flu virus since the 2009 pandemic. It spreads mainly through respiratory droplets released when an infected person coughs, sneezes or speaks. Most people recover within approximately one week without requiring hospital treatment.

However, doctors warn that older adults, pregnant women, young children and those with chronic conditions such as diabetes, heart disease or lung disease face greater risk of complications including pneumonia and respiratory distress. Dr Niraj Kumar of ShardaCare-Healthcity in Greater Noida noted that the current season is showing a wider range of symptoms in some patients, including persistent cough, high fever, body ache, fatigue and gastrointestinal symptoms such as diarrhoea.

What Diaspora Travelers Should Know

For Indian Americans and NRIs planning travel to Delhi during the monsoon season, the H1N1 surge adds a layer of health planning. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommends annual flu vaccination as the primary prevention measure. Travelers should consult their physicians about the current season's flu vaccine before departure, carry hand sanitiser, and seek medical attention promptly if they develop fever, breathing difficulty or persistent symptoms during or after a visit.

Seasonal influenza, including H1N1, is predominantly a mild and self-limiting respiratory illness among otherwise healthy people, Bahl said — but early medical consultation remains important, particularly when fever or breathing difficulty persists.
